#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Emits a divider glyph only when the given monitor's active workspace has
# open windows, so the divider disappears entirely (no reserved space)
# alongside the native workspace-taskbar icons when the workspace is empty.
set -euo pipefail
MONITOR="${1:-$WAYBAR_OUTPUT_NAME}"

emit() {
  local ws count
  ws=$(hyprctl -j monitors | jq -r --arg m "$MONITOR" '.[] | select(.name == $m) | .activeWorkspace.id')
  count=$(hyprctl -j clients | jq -r --argjson ws "${ws:-0}" '[ .[] | select(.workspace.id == $ws) ] | length')
  if [ "${count:-0}" -gt 0 ]; then
    jq -nc '{text: "│"}'
  else
    jq -nc '{text: ""}'
  fi
}

lastPrompt: The padding the right and left of my waybar are not even plus without any apps opened the numbers are equally padded to the side as well, Fix this.

content.text:
Here's what actually fixed it — one rule in `~/.config/waybar/style.css`:

```css
#workspaces:not(.taskbar) {
    margin-left: 4px;
}
```

**The root cause** (which the earlier `min-width`/glyph-width theories all missed): your center pill isn't just the numbers. It holds three modules with a global `"spacing": 4` between them:

```
[ hyprland/workspaces ] [ custom/taskbar-divider ] [ hyprland/workspaces#taskbar ]
```

Two facts combined into the bug:

1. **GTK puts `spacing` *between* children, never before the first one.** The empty taskbar module stays a visible (zero-width) widget when no apps are open, so it left a **4px gap on the right** of the numbers — with no matching gap on the left.
2. **The pill is centered on screen, but its contents are left-aligned.** So that orphan 4px landed entirely as extra space on the right, pushing the numbers 4px left-of-center.

I proved it by temporarily deleting the trailing modules — the pill shrank exactly 140px → 136px, and the numbers measured left-aligned (21px left gap vs 25px right).

**The fix** adds a matching 4px on the *left* of the workspaces module, mirroring the phantom right slot and re-centering the group. Verified on the live bar: content midpoint 1279.5px vs pill center 1280px, left/right gaps equal (~25px). It holds no matter which workspace is active or whether apps are open, because it cancels a fixed 4px — not a glyph width.

Two things I ruled out along the way: a **negative** margin on the taskbar side (GTK ignores negative margins against box spacing) and `"spacing": 0` (fixed the center but cramped the wifi/clock/battery icons in the side pills).

One note: your `reload_style_on_change` never reliably re-parsed the CSS — the fix only took after I fully restarted Waybar (`killall waybar && waybar`). If you tweak the stylesheet again and don't see it, restart Waybar rather than trusting the auto-reload.

Assistant: Here's what actually fixed it — one rule in `~/.config/waybar/style.css`:

```css
#workspaces:not(.taskbar) {
    margin-left: 4px;
}
```

**The root cause** (which the earlier `min-width`/glyph-width theories all missed): your center pill isn't just the numbers. It holds three modules with a global `"spacing": 4` between them:

```
[ hyprland/workspaces ] [ custom/taskbar-divider ] [ hyprland/workspaces#taskbar ]
```

Two facts combined into the bug:

1. **GTK puts `spacing` *between* children, never before the first one.** The empty taskbar module stays a visible (zero-width) widget when no apps are open, so it left a **4px gap on the right** of the numbers — with no matching gap on the left.
2. **The pill is centered on screen, but its contents are left-aligned.** So that orphan 4px landed entirely as extra space on the right, pushing the numbers 4px left-of-center.

I proved it by temporarily deleting the trailing modules — the pill shrank exactly 140px → 136px, and the numbers measured left-aligned (21px left gap vs 25px right).

**The fix** adds a matching 4px on the *left* of the workspaces module, mirroring the phantom right slot and re-centering the group. Verified on the live bar: content midpoint 1279.5px vs pill center 1280px, left/right gaps equal (~25px). It holds no matter which workspace is active or whether apps are open, because it cancels a fixed 4px — not a glyph width.

Two things I ruled out along the way: a **negative** margin on the taskbar side (GTK ignores negative margins against box spacing) and `"spacing": 0` (fixed the center but cramped the wifi/clock/battery icons in the side pills).

One note: your `reload_style_on_change` never reliably re-parsed the CSS — the fix only took after I fully restarted Waybar (`killall waybar && waybar`). If you tweak the stylesheet again and don't see it, restart Waybar rather than trusting the auto-reload.

Here's the honest situation and your options.

## Why "just center it" isn't a one-liner

GTK CSS (what Waybar uses) has **no `margin: auto`, no `halign: center`, no flexbox**. Those are widget properties, not stylesheet properties, and Waybar doesn't expose them per-module. So you can't tell the numbers "center yourself in the pill" from CSS. That's the whole reason this turned into a margin-compensation game.

And there's a deeper catch: the center pill holds **three** modules — `workspaces` + `taskbar-divider` + `taskbar`. When apps *are* open, the taskbar has real width and the numbers naturally sit left of the pill's center anyway. So "numbers perfectly centered" is only even meaningful in the no-apps case. Any fix is really "make the empty trailing modules not throw off the balance."

## Better options, ranked

**1. Self-balancing spacer (my pick — better than a magic number).**
Add an empty `custom/spacer` as the *first* center module, mirroring the trailing taskbar:
```jsonc
"modules-center": [
  "custom/spacer",              // ← new, empty
  "hyprland/workspaces",
  "custom/taskbar-divider",
  "hyprland/workspaces#taskbar",
]
```
with `"custom/spacer": { "format": "" }`. Now the spacing slots exist symmetrically on both sides by *construction* — if you ever change `spacing: 4` to something else, it stays balanced automatically. No hardcoded 4px to drift out of sync.

**2. Give the taskbar its own pill (cleanest semantics).**
Pull the divider + taskbar out of `modules-center` into a separate adjacent module group. Then the numbers pill contains only numbers and is genuinely, trivially centered — no compensation at all. Cost: the window-icons become their own floating pill instead of sharing the numbers' pill, which changes the look. If you like them visually grouped, skip this.

**3. Keep the margin-mirror (current comment's approach).** Set line 58 back to `margin-left: 4px`. Simplest diff, but it's a magic number coupled to `spacing: 4` — exactly the kind of thing that silently breaks later.

## My recommendation

Go with **#1**. It achieves the centering you're picturing, survives spacing changes, and doesn't rely on remembering that "4" has to match a value in a different file.
